subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests make persisted session defaults an intentional behavior, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make global policy the ceiling
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear, clamp, or ignore stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade coverage.

options.title: Keep persisted session defaults
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset/doctor first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make global policy the ceiling
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear, clamp, or ignore stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history trail for the original `/exec` session override feature and the current precedence tests.
